module_microarchitecture.name: active_aero_ctrl_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single synchronous top-level supervisor with registered request issuance, response qualification, deterministic command synthesis, clamp/rate-limit post-processing, and safety fallback arbitration around an external surrogate transaction contract.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use simple cycle-by-cycle control with a pending-request flag, a monotonic req_id counter, a timeout age/down counter, and combinational qualification of flow envelope, response match, and integrity conditions. Avoid complex FSMs; implement status/fault encoding directly from the current supervisory conditions and registered state.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Register configuration metadata, the latest accepted flow sample, outstanding req_id, pending request indicator, timeout counter, safe default actuator value, previous actuator command for optional rate limiting, trace registers, and sticky/pulse fault indicators. On synchronous active-low reset, initialize all state to safe fallback, clear pending and counters, and drive outputs to safe values.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive req_valid and the request bundle only when a valid flow sample is accepted and issuance is permitted. Drive actuator_cmd from the selected command path unless fallback is active, in which case drive the safe default value and deassert actuator_valid. Generate stale_reject, timeout_fault, cmd_clamped, status_code, fault_code, trace_req_id, and trace_rsp_id as registered or carefully controlled synchronous outputs consistent with the current transaction state.
ownership_notes: Safe fallback dominates all normal command updates whenever reset, envelope violation, timeout, stale/mismatched response, or integrity failure is present.
Recovery from fallback is synchronous and deterministic, requiring a valid accepted request-response cycle and cleared safety conditions.
All arithmetic and comparisons are fixed-point or integer and synthesizable.
The external DoMINO surrogate remains outside RTL and is referenced only through the visible request/response ports.

fsm_intent.description: No explicit multi-state FSM is required. The implementation intent is a small set of synchronous supervisory registers and condition-based output qualification rather than a coded state machine.

output_mapping: req_id driven from the next/issued request sequence value
req_geometry_source/formats/id forwarded from registered geometry metadata
req_stream_velocity_mps and req_flow_valid forwarded from the accepted flow sample
actuator_cmd driven from the clamped/rate-limited synthesized command unless fallback overrides to the safe default
actuator_valid asserted only when a validated response produces a usable command and fallback is clear
fallback_active driven from safety-supervision conditions and held until recovery conditions are met
stale_reject asserted on mismatched/stale response handling per implementation policy
timeout_fault asserted on timeout expiry handling per implementation policy
cmd_clamped asserted when the command candidate saturates at min/max bounds
status_code and fault_code encoded from idle/pending/accepted/fallback/fault and none/stale/timeout/envelope/integrity/clamp conditions
trace_req_id and trace_rsp_id exposed for debug/traceability

sequencing_notes: Capture a flow sample only when flow_valid is asserted and stream_velocity_mps is within the parameterized envelope, with mandatory support for 20..55 inclusive.
Issue a request only when no pending request blocks issuance and the supervisor is not in a blocking fault condition.
Increment req_id monotonically on each accepted request transaction and mark the request pending in the same synchronous update.
While pending, increment or decrement the timeout counter each clock cycle until a matching response is accepted or the timeout condition is reached.
Accept a response only when rsp_valid is high, rsp_id matches the outstanding req_id, flow_field_valid is asserted, and integrity/freshness checks pass.
Discard mismatched responses and assert stale_reject for the transaction; ignore responses arriving after timeout and assert timeout_fault.
On accepted response, update trace_rsp_id, generate the command candidate from validated payloads, then apply clamp and optional rate limiting before registering actuator_cmd.
If fallback is active, suppress actuator_valid and hold actuator_cmd at the safe default value until synchronous recovery conditions are satisfied.
cfg_clear_sticky_faults clears sticky stale_reject and timeout_fault indicators when sticky mode is implemented; otherwise those indicators may behave as pulses.
timing_notes: All logic is synchronous to clk with active-low synchronous reset_n.
Use registered state for request tracking, timeout supervision, previous command storage, and trace outputs to keep long control paths timing-friendly.
Avoid combinational loops and X-dependent gating; all handshakes must rely on explicit valid qualifiers only.
Clamp and optional rate-limit logic should be implemented with compare/select and saturating add/sub logic, allowing a single registered actuator update per accepted response.
Reset release must not create asynchronous transitions; recovery from fallback is deterministic on clock edges only.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
